title: Conservation laws in particle interactions; Pair production and annihilation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for Edexcel A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: P05-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; P05-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; P05-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; P05-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: P03-1#N.3, P05-1#N.2, P03-1#N.8, P05-1#N.4, P03-1#N.13a, P05-1#N.9, P05-1#N.10, P05-1#N.13.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Rest energy
items.clue: Quantity linked to mass that becomes photons: 0.511 MeV for one electron.

items.label: Positron
items.clue: Written e⁺: it meets an electron at low speed to give two 0.511 MeV gamma photons.

items.label: Antiparticle
items.clue: General name for a counterpart with the same mass but opposite charge; every type has one.

items.label: Annihilation
items.clue: Event in which matter meets its opposite counterpart and both turn into photons, usually two.

questions.stem: In a decay, an up quark changes into a down quark. Which of these must also be emitted for charge to be conserved?
questions.explanation: +⅔ = −⅓ + 1 + 0. The quark loses one unit of charge, so a particle with +1e must leave: this is β⁺ decay.

questions.stem: An electron and a positron annihilate, producing two photons. Which quantity is different after the annihilation from before it?
questions.explanation: Photons have no rest mass. The pair's mass has been converted to photon energy, but energy and momentum are conserved.

questions.stem: A student proposes that a free neutron decays into a proton and an electron and nothing else: n → p + e⁻. Which conservation law that holds in all nuclear decays would this proposal break?

options.text: Charge, since two charged particles would come from one neutral particle
Baryon number, since a neutron would be replaced by a proton
Lepton number, since the number of electrons and neutrinos would rise
Mass, since the proton and electron have less mass than the neutron

questions.stem: A muon and an antimuon, both almost at rest, annihilate to produce two photons. The rest energy of a muon is 105.7 MeV. What is the wavelength of each photon?
Which of these proposed interactions is forbidden by a conservation law?
questions.explanation: Q 0 = 0 and B 1 = 1, but L: 0 + 1 = +1 before, 0 − 1 = −1 after. Electron capture emits a neutrino, νₑ, not an antineutrino.

questions.stem: The tau lepton has a mass of 1.78 GeV/c². What is its mass in kilograms?
A photon creates a proton–antiproton pair. The rest energy of a proton is 938 MeV. What is the minimum frequency of the photon?
An electron and a positron, each with 0.30 MeV of kinetic energy, collide head-on and annihilate into two photons. The rest energy of an electron is 0.511 MeV. What is the energy of each photon?
questions.explanation: Head-on with equal energies, the total momentum is zero, so the two photons have equal energies and fly apart in opposite directions. Each: 0.511 + 0.30 = 0.81 MeV.
